children: Preface to the English Edition
英文版前言

This book is the culmination of a research career I began in the 1970s, which, over the course of many years, led me to ask questions about the meaning of the word “market.” The word itself does not seem complicated, yet its significance remained a mystery to me for a long time.
本书是我自20世纪70年代开始的研究生涯的结晶。多年来，这项工作引导我不断追问“市场”一词的含义。这个词本身似乎并不复杂，但它的意义在很长一段时间里对我来说始终是个谜。

I am aware that my feelings are not shared by the majority. Many are convinced they know what a market is because they are told they live in market economies. Others trust in experts who have been writing on the topic over the course of several centuries. One of the objectives of this book is to persuade the reader that we need to reexamine our most deeply held convictions.
我意识到，大多数人与我的感受并不相同。许多人确信自己知道市场是什么，因为他们被告知自己生活在市场经济之中。另一些人则信任那些几个世纪以来一直撰写相关主题的专家。本书的目标之一，是说服读者重新审视我们最根深蒂固的信念。

The feeling of false familiarity is not the only obstacle to fully understanding how markets are formed and how they transform. With so many challenges to the future of our societies, whether it be climate change, ecological damage, human rights, growing inequality, or geopolitical confrontations, it can feel like markets are of secondary importance. Circumstances conspire to edge markets out of our attention and dissuade us from deepening our exploration of what they can do or make happen (in French,
faire-faire
虚假的熟悉感并不是充分理解市场如何形成、如何转变的唯一障碍。面对我们社会未来的诸多挑战——气候变化、生态破坏、人权、日益加剧的不平等或地缘政治对抗——人们会觉得市场只具有次要意义。各种情势合力把市场挤出了我们的注意范围，也阻止我们深入探究市场能够做什么、能够促使什么发生（法文为

This book takes a gamble in the opposite direction. It takes seriously the famous affirmation of economist and anthropologist Karl Polanyi when he evokes the possible role of markets in the future: “The end of market society means in no way the absence of markets. These continue, in various fashions, to ensure the freedom of the consumer, to indicate the shifting of demand, to influence producers’ income, and to serve as an instrument of accountancy, while ceasing altogether to be an organ of economic self-regulation.”
本书朝相反方向押注。它认真对待经济学家兼人类学家卡尔·波兰尼（Karl Polanyi）在设想市场未来可能扮演的角色时所作的著名论断：“市场社会的终结绝不意味着市场的缺席。市场仍将以各种方式继续保障消费者的自由，显示需求的变化，影响生产者的收入，并充当核算的工具，同时完全不再充当经济自我调节的器官。”

To my ear, Polanyi’s message rings crystal clear. He refuses to treat markets as either straightforward instruments that should be regulated or as harmful institutions that we should be rid of. According to him, we should neither fight markets nor consider them mere instruments. Instead, he invites us to preserve the strengths of markets, with their capacity to contribute to realizing collective and individual well-being, while at the same time ensuring the preservation of values that are deemed to be essential. In his words, “Civic liberties, private enterprise and wage-system fused into a pattern of life which favored moral freedom and independence of mind. . . . We must try to maintain by all means in our power these high values inherited from the market-economy which collapsed.”

在我看来，波兰尼的讯息再清楚不过。他既拒绝把市场当作应当被监管的简单工具，也拒绝把市场当作应当被清除的有害制度。按照他的看法，我们既不应与市场作战，也不应把市场仅仅视为工具。相反，他邀请我们保留市场的力量，保留市场有助于实现集体与个体福祉的能力，同时确保那些被视为根本的价值得到维护。用他的话说：“公民自由、私人企业与工资制度融合成一种生活方式，这种生活方式有利于道德自由与心灵独立……我们必须尽一切力量维护这些从已经崩溃的市场经济中继承下来的崇高价值。”

Polanyi is correct. In economic life, commercial practices will remain essential because there is no substitute; they play a role no other institution is able to hold. To advance this claim, I have pursued a simple strategy. I take up the basic query that imposed itself on me at the beginning of my research career and has preoccupied me ever since: “What is a market?” In every study I have ever undertaken, the market has been there, like a weighty, but indecipherable shadow. Everywhere and nowhere, I could feel its presence, even if I could never grasp it. The dissatisfaction I experienced had nothing to do with dogmatic considerations or disciplinary loyalty. No matter what I read, I found no definitions that coincided with my empirical observations. The discomfort was unleashed during the first study I ever did on the development of an electric vehicle.

波兰尼是对的。在经济生活中，商业实践仍将不可或缺，因为没有替代品；它们扮演着任何其他制度都无法承担的角色。为了推进这一主张，我采取了一个简单的策略。我重新拾起研究生涯之初就强加于我、此后一直萦绕于我的基本问题：“什么是市场？”在我做过的每一项研究中，市场都在那里，像一道沉重却无法辨认的阴影。它无处不在又无处可寻；我能感觉到它的存在，却始终无法把握它。我所经历的不满与教条考虑或学科忠诚无关。无论读什么，我都找不到与我的经验观察相吻合的定义。这种不适在我最早开展的电动汽车开发研究中充分显露出来。

It is amusing to remember that at the end of the nineteenth century, a world record for speed was set by a vehicle called “La Jamais Contente” (The Never Happy), powered by a 750-kilogram lead battery. Less remembered are the generously financed projects, launched in several countries in the 1970s, notably in France, to give electric vehicles a second chance.
回想起来颇有趣味：19世纪末，一辆名为“永不满足”（La Jamais Contente）的汽车创下了速度世界纪录，它由一块重750公斤的铅电池驱动。较少被人记住的是20世纪70年代在若干国家、尤其是法国启动的资助慷慨的项目，它们想给电动汽车第二次机会。

The Club of Rome’s report put ecological questions and growth on the agenda of the highest circles of administration and power. By 1971, a minister of the environment was named in France for the first time. In the domain of industry, the objective was to bring forth solutions to the problems posed by pollution and the risk of exhausting combustible fossil fuel resources. A call for concerted action was issued by the state to overturn scientific and technical barriers standing in the way of alternative viable markets. Collaborations were organized between all of the stakeholders, from university researchers to consumer representatives, industry leaders, technical centers, government ministers, and so on. Efforts to develop an alternative to thermal engines centered on several types of fuel cells whose remarkable performance had already been demonstrated in space. Back then, we were already speaking of a hydrogen economy powered by nuclear electricity.

罗马俱乐部的报告把生态问题与增长提上了最高行政与权力圈的议程。到1971年，法国首次任命了环境部长。在工业领域，目标是提出解决方案，应对污染以及可燃化石燃料资源枯竭的风险。国家发出协同行动的号召，以清除阻碍替代性可行市场的科学与技术壁垒。所有利益相关者都被组织起来合作，从大学研究人员到消费者代表、产业领袖、技术中心、政府部长等等。寻找内燃机替代方案的努力集中在几种燃料电池上，这些电池的卓越性能已在太空得到验证。当时，人们已经在谈论由核能发电驱动的氢经济。

I received funding that assured me freedom and autonomy for three years and became what we would now call an embedded researcher. I was granted unlimited access to archives and the possibility of collaborating with teams of researchers and engineers working on the project. Progressive and modernizing French technocrats felt that including a sociologist and general engineer, one with additional training in economics, would surely boost the program! This is how I found myself at the heart of the reactor where social structures are transformed, in a kind of crucible where the ingredients that form what we call society are melted down and reformed, all while being pounded by often violent controversies between groups who saw the future differently. Through it all, I was surrounded by markets, either those that existed or those that were slated to exist.

我获得了一笔资助，保证我三年内拥有自由与自主，并成为我们今天所称的“嵌入式研究者”。我获准无限制地查阅档案，并有机会与参与项目的研究人员和工程师团队合作。进步主义、现代化取向的法国技术官僚认为，引入一位社会学家兼通才型工程师、且受过经济学额外训练的人，必定会推动该计划！就这样，我发现自己置身于反应堆的核心：社会结构在那里被转化，仿佛置身于一个坩埚，构成我们所谓社会的各种成分在其中熔化、重塑，同时不断受到群体之间往往激烈的争论的冲击，这些群体对未来的看法各不相同。在这一切之中，我被市场包围着，无论是已经存在的市场，还是预定将要出现的市场。

I noticed that an economist colleague of similar training who did not have my access to the field of action was relying on standard tools to analyze and predict whether the transition from thermal to electric cars would eventually occur. He took into account all of the available variables and ended up with the conclusion that he was unable to make a serious prediction about anything. What completely escaped him were the observations I made in my daily environment: the profound uncertainty when knotting together economic, social, technical, political, and social concerns, as well as the multiple temporal horizons of the projects underway.
我注意到，一位受过类似训练、但无法像我一样进入行动现场的经济学家同事，正依赖标准工具来分析和预测从内燃机汽车向电动汽车的转型最终是否会发生。他考虑了所有可获得的变量，最后得出的结论却是：他无法对任何事情作出严肃预测。他完全错过的是我在日常环境中作出的观察：经济、社会、技术、政治等方面的关切交织在一起时的深刻不确定性，以及进行中项目的多重时间视域。

In the moment, many clever people announced what the market logic was and where things were going. Yet from where I stood, all I could see was a chaotic construction site, sciences in the making, commercial practices in the making, from which structured markets might one day emerge, but only if circumstances proved favorable. Very quickly, I further understood that distinguishing between
markets in the making
and
made markets
makes no sense. There are only
markets in the making

that are being transformed more or less intensively. Whether in my work on the treatments developed for rare diseases or on innovation in services, every one of the studies I have carried out reconfirms this original finding.
当时，许多聪明人宣称市场逻辑是什么、事情将走向何方。然而从我所站的位置看，我只看到一个混乱的工地：形成中的科学、形成中的商业实践；结构化的市场也许有一天会从中出现，但前提是环境有利。很快，我进一步明白：区分“
形成中的市场
已形成的市场
”毫无意义。只存在
形成中的市场
，它们正以或强或弱的程度被转变。无论是我关于罕见病治疗方法的研究，还是关于服务创新的研究，我做过的每一项研究都再次确认了这一最初的发现。

The bottom line is that economics, sociology, and anthropology all share the objective of moving themselves as far away as possible from operating markets in order to simplify their representation in theory. This means that researchers today continue to face the same challenge, the same confusion as I did. This book seeks to give firm guidance on how to dissolve the tension between academic theories and what is happening in the field.
归根结底，经济学、社会学和人类学都有一个共同目标：尽可能远离实际运作的市场，以便在理论中简化对市场的表述。这意味着，今天的研究者仍然面对与我相同的挑战、相同的困惑。本书试图给出明确的指引，说明如何化解学术理论与现场实际发生之事之间的张力。

What can we hope for by plunging ourselves into the effervescence of commercial practices instead of seeing them in vague outlines from the great distance imposed by abstraction? In other words, what is the value added by coming down into the empirical weeds? At the conceptual level, my approach will not only give us a more realistic understanding of how markets work, but it will open our eyes to everything that permits a functioning market to be formed, established, maintained, and transformed. Having looked more closely, we will discover that the concepts of competition, goods, and innovation need to be significantly reworked.
如果我们投身于商业实践的沸腾之中，而不是从抽象所强加的巨大距离外模糊地观望，我们能指望得到什么？换言之，深入经验生活的杂草丛中，能带来什么附加价值？在概念层面，我的方法不仅会让我们更现实地理解市场如何运作，还会让我们看清一切使一个运作中的市场得以形成、建立、维持和转变的条件。更仔细地观察之后，我们会发现竞争、物品和创新的概念都需要大幅重做。

A second result, the most important, in my opinion, is to dissociate two big terms that get confused with one another: “markets” and “capitalism.” The notion of “market agencement” presented in this book allows for this conceptual disintrication because it closely observes the substance and materiality of market practices. The confusion that prevails today dissipates the diversity of forms in market organizations. The tricky dissociation I will make in the book is now much easier to defend, since recent works, such as those by Katharina Pistor,

or older ones such as those by historians of accounting techniques or credit practices, make it possible to better characterize market arrangements that are specifically capitalist, distinguishing them from those that are not.
第二个结果——在我看来也是最重要的结果——是把两个常被混为一谈的大词拆开：“市场”与“资本主义”。本书提出的“市场装配”概念使这种概念上的解缠成为可能，因为它近距离观察市场实践的实质与物质性。今天盛行的混淆遮蔽了市场组织形式的多样性。我在本书中要做的这种棘手区分，如今更容易辩护，因为晚近的著作——例如凯瑟琳娜·皮斯托（Katharina Pistor）的作品
——以及更早的会计技术史或信贷实践史研究，使我们能够更好地刻画那些特定属于资本主义的市场安排，并把它们与非资本主义的市场安排区分开来。

There remain a number of difficulties in the approach I am proposing. Although I will make the strong case that we must make the conceptual adjustments outlined above, carrying out the empirical research to support these changes is no light task. The materials most accessible to me come from current economic forms; thus, these examples are privileged. I have tried to develop the generality of the concept but acknowledge that more work needs to be done.
我所提出的方法仍有许多困难。尽管我会强有力地论证我们必须作出上述概念调整，但要开展支持这些变化的经验研究绝非易事。我最容易获得的材料来自当前的经济形式，因此这些例子受到偏重。我试图拓展这一概念的普适性，但也承认还需要做更多工作。

Another set of difficulties relates to politics. A central notion in my work is “matters of concern.” The framings described in this book that lead to commercial transactions are also arrangements that shape behaviors. The behavioral effect incites and nourishes movements of resistance that level critiques. As I will emphasize, researchers need to treat these movements carefully and give them their place in the analysis. As I will argue, critique is not external to the market, but is rather its dynamic heartbeat: it generates the motion that keeps markets fresh and alive. This does not imply that researchers should be dispassionate observers. In the final chapter of the book, I will make the case that it is altogether laudable for academics to participate in generating and expressing matters of concern. The first version of this book was published in France in 2017. The translation was no smooth ride, since the original text alternated between theoretical developments (which I recognize were somewhat arduous) and more vivid descriptions to illustrate how the analysis might work. I would like to thank Olivia Custer for having conveyed these movements in tone and style without ever sacrificing the coherence of the whole.

另一组困难与政治有关。我工作中的一个核心概念是“关切事项”。本书描述的那些导向商业交易的框定，同时也是塑造行为的安排。这种行为效应会激发并滋养抵抗运动，后者提出批评。正如我将强调的，研究者需要谨慎对待这些运动，并在分析中给它们一席之地。正如我将论证的，批评并非外在于市场，而是市场跳动的心脏：它产生运动，使市场保持新鲜与活力。这并不意味着研究者应当保持超然、不动感情。在本书最后一章，我会论证：学者参与关切事项的生成与表达完全值得称赞。本书第一版于2017年在法国出版。翻译并非一帆风顺，因为原文在理论展开（我承认有些艰深）与更生动的描述之间交替，以说明分析如何运作。我要感谢奥利维娅·卡斯特（Olivia Custer）在语气与风格上传达了这些运动，同时从未牺牲整体的连贯性。

Translation is a difficult and risky art form. It frequently requires transposing and reformulating ideas for audiences with different experiences and disciplinary backgrounds. This interpretive work was done with remarkable patience by Martha Poon, to whom I express my profound gratitude. Over the course of our exchange, entire passages were rewritten to the point where it crossed my mind that a second edition might be issued in French by translating backward from the English one. I will be saving my energies instead for a second volume, which will explore the process of constructing what might be called a “good” market agencement.
翻译是一门困难而冒险的艺术。它常常需要为拥有不同经验和学科背景的读者转换并重新表述思想。这项解释工作由玛莎·潘（Martha Poon）以非凡的耐心完成，我向她表达深切谢意。在我们的交流过程中，整段文字被重写，以至于我一度想到可以从英文版倒译回法文，出版一个法文第二版。不过，我宁愿把精力留给第二卷，那将探讨如何建构一个或许可称为“好的”市场装配。
Let me close by profoundly acknowledging Michel Feher, who believed in this book and unambivalently supported its translation. —
Michel Callon, 2020
